messages:
Maya: Heads up — after landing the kernel-selection heuristic tweak (prefer_fused=true) we’re seeing a regression on the 8xA100 TP+PP inference job. Throughput down ~18%, and traces show long gaps where all-reduce is waiting for kernels to finish. :eyes:

Jon: ugh. Can you paste the profiling snippet / nvprof timeline? Is this only with CUDA Graph capture enabled?

Maya: quick dump from nsight-ncu (trimmed):
```
Timeline summary:
- GPU0 compute active 0-120ms, idle 120-210ms
- NCCL all-reduce start 115ms, wait for kernel completion, duration 90ms
Allreduce stalls correlate with kernel launch lag on GPUs 2..7.
Kernel selection: fused_attention_kernel_v2 chosen for seq=1024, batch=8
Previously used: attention_v1 + split-kernel path
```
Seems like fused kernel has higher per-launch latency and prevents overlap. Graph capture appears to replay on the same per-GPU external stream which ends up serialized with NCCL stream.

Devin: That matches a hypothesis: the fused kernel increases single-GPU runtime so the runtime scheduler queues NCCL on a different stream expecting compute overlap, but CUDA Graph replay reuses cudaStreamCaptureMode and serializes the sequence. If the capture binds the external stream, the NCCL enqueues after the fused kernel finishes on that stream. Did we change stream affinity or stream priorities in the heuristic?

Maya: We added an affinity hint: kernel_affinity=prefer_high_priority_stream for fused kernels. Might be making capture pick a low-priority fallback stream at capture time.

Ryan: Reproduced locally without KV-prefetch: same pattern. With KV-prefetch enabled it gets worse because prefetch does host-sync to warm KV then capture triggers another sync. Quick log: 
```
[GPU0] fused_attention_kernel_v2 launch time = 9.2ms
[NCCL] allreduce wait = 72ms
[KV] prefetch host-sync = 4ms (happens before capture)
```
When we disable graph capture the overlap improves and throughput returns to baseline.

perf-bot: auto-profile link: https://perf.internal/profiles/1712349999 (contains full ncu capture + kernel timelines). :robot_face:

Sophie: Two actionable experiments: 1) pin fused kernels to a dedicated compute stream and set NCCL on high-priority stream (explicit queues) 2) disable stream reuse during graph capture (force new stream per capture) or fall back to non-capture path for seq>512.

Jon: Can we try an immediate guard: if fused kernel latency > 6ms then prefer split-kernel path (even if slightly slower per-op) to preserve comm/compute overlap? That would be a cheap heuristic change.

Devin: Also check KV cache warmup: if prefetch does host->device memcpy synchronously before capture, that host sync can flush CUDA stream semantics and create an implicit barrier. We should ensure prefetch uses async memcpy on separate stream and that capture excludes the host-sync region.

Maya: Good plan. I’ll run two quick experiments this morning: A) revert kernel selection for seq>768 B) disable graph capture for the prefetched KV path. I’ll post perf numbers.

Ryan: If you want a fast toggle I added runtime flags: --serve.kernel_policy=legacy_or_split and --serve.capture_mode=off_for_prefetch. Use them in canary.

Maya: Thanks — starting canary now. Rolling 10% to dedicated pool. Will share numbers in ~30m.

Sophie: If canary confirms, we should make a short-term rollback and open a follow-up to rethink the kernel-latency awareness in the graph-capture planner. This is QoS-impacting. :warning:

Maya: Canary result (30m): revert-to-split restored throughput to baseline; disabling capture on prefetched path improved latency tail (p99 down ~120ms). Will open PR to gate fused-kernel selection by "capture-safe" flag and add unit test that runs a mini capture + NCCL microbenchmark.

Jon: Great — add an integration test that asserts no increase in allreduce wait in CI (narrow threshold). Also note the perf regression in the release notes.

Maya: Filed issue IR-4312, and PR incoming with the heuristic guard + docs. Closing thread once PR merges.
